items.title: Known-count search by randomized Grover iteration
items.statement_or_definition: Input N=2^n, exact count t and standard bit-query access to f=1_M. If t=0, return `none` with no query. If t>N/2, perform at most nine independent rounds: initialize a fresh address register to |0^n⟩ and apply H^⊗n to prepare |s⟩, measure x, make one standard bit query to verify f(x), and return x if f(x)=1; after nine failures return `fail`. If 0<t≤N/2, compute K as the least positive integer with tK²≥N by binary search: initialize lo=0 and hi=2^ceil(n/2), and while hi−lo>1 set mid=floor((lo+hi)/2), replace hi by mid if t·mid²≥N and otherwise replace lo by mid. Set b to the least nonnegative integer with 2^b≥K. For each of nine independent rounds draw b fair bits to obtain j∈{0,…,2^b−1}; if j≥K, reject this round without a query. Otherwise prepare a fresh |s⟩=H^⊗n|0^n⟩, prepare a response qubit in |−⟩ for phase kickback, apply `alg-qa-11-grover-iterate` exactly j times with R_s=2|s⟩⟨s|−I, measure x and make one standard bit query to verify f(x), returning x if marked. After nine unsuccessful rounds return `fail`.

Show b=ceil(log₂K) and rejection sampling accepts with probability K/2^b≥1/2, with accepted j uniform on {0,…,K−1}.
Use fresh independent random bits, fresh uniform-state preparation and fresh response ancilla per attempt; rejected rounds use no oracle query.

Each Grover iterate is the QA11 bit-query-to-phase-kickback subalgorithm; each measured candidate is verified by a separate standard bit query.
For t>N/2, the nine direct uniform samples are finite and each succeeds with probability t/N>1/2.
